headline: OpenHands can write and network by default, but LightZero is non-runnable and read-only, so the main risks are bounded to OpenHands-side leakage, conflicts, and compliance gaps.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no shared channel or I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject OpenHands by default. OpenHands can ingest files and MCP content, but the pair lacks a documented bridge from LightZero to OpenHands. Any prompt-injection pathway would require unusual manual transfer or external wiring.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies LightZero output into OpenHands prompts or files
IF an MCP server is configured to relay LightZero-generated content into OpenHands
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting model outputs into OpenHands prompts
Disable untrusted MCP servers
Use a provenance label on imported text
Review any file imported from LightZero before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no files and has no network egress, while OpenHands reads and writes runtime files and may send data to a configured model provider. The pair does not show a shared workspace by default, so leakage is limited unless an operator mounts sensitive files into OpenHands.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF OpenHands is configured with a third-party model provider
mitigations: Mount only non-sensitive files
Use a local model provider
Rotate any exposed API keys
Unshare the runtime volume after use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use the network, so it cannot contend with OpenHands for mutable resources. OpenHands can modify files and git state inside its runtime, but there is no overlapping write surface with LightZero in the profiles, making conflict unlikely.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mounted volume
IF OpenHands instances are run concurrently against the same runtime directory
mitigations: Use separate runtime directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same volume
Enable per-task workspace isolation
Lock shared files before editing

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero does not produce downstream actions or verified outputs that OpenHands is documented to consume automatically. OpenHands has an agent loop and can act on files, but without a documented ingestion path from LightZero, cascading error is mainly a manual workflow risk rather than a default one.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are manually treated as authoritative input to OpenHands
IF OpenHands is instructed to execute actions based on unverified LightZero results
mitigations: Require human review before acting on LightZero outputs
Add a verification step in OpenHands prompts
Separate analysis and execution tasks
Log source provenance for imported results

E_compliance.rationale: LightZero is open-source game-playing software with no touched data classes, while OpenHands handles files in a runtime sandbox and model-provider API keys. The profiles do not show a residency or regulated-data mismatch by default, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen inputs and providers.
conditions: IF regulated data is mounted into OpenHands
IF the configured model provider stores prompts outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Do not mount regulated data
Use a provider with an acceptable DPA
Purge runtime files after the task
Keep API keys out of shared volumes
